This is usually [[ISO 843|transliterated letter-for-letter]] back into the [[Latin alphabet]] as ''Antetokounmpo''.}} July 18, 1992{{cite web|title=THANASIS ANTETOKOUNMPO Born: 7/18/92|url=http://stats.nba.com/player/#!/203648/|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401124428/http://stats.nba.com/player/#!/203648/|archive-date=April 1, 2016|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|title=Athanasios ANTETOKOUNMPO Date of Birth 18 Jul 1992 Nationality: GRE|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/Page/d3698440-ce75-4059-90f1-39e365e08ec4/d7b6e7bd-2867-932d-6bbe-d96318b827af|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=September 4, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231118011441/https://www.fiba.basketball/en/Page/d3698440-ce75-4059-90f1-39e365e08ec4/d7b6e7bd-2867-932d-6bbe-d96318b827af|archive-date=November 18, 2023|url-status=live}}) is a Nigerian-Greek professional [[basketball]] player for [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. At the international stage, he has represented the [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national team]] since 2016. Listed at 6 feet 7 inches, he plays at the [[small forward]] and [[power forward]] positions. He won back-to-back [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] championships with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] in 2018 and 2019 and the [[NBA Finals|NBA championship]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]. He is the older brother of two-time [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|NBA MVP]] [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] as well as [[Kostas Antetokounmpo|Kostas]] and [[Alex Antetokounmpo|Alex]]. Giannis and Alex are both former Bucks teammates of Thanasis, with all three playing on the same roster in the [[2025–26_Milwaukee_Bucks_season|2025-26 season]].{{cite web |last1=Toporek |first1=Bryan |title=How the Milwaukee Bucks' nepotism could wind up pushing Giannis Antetokounmpo away |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/milwaukee-bucks-nepotism-could-wind-181458036.html |website=Yahoo! Sports |access-date=1 September 2026}} ==Early career== Antetokounmpo was born in Athens, the second of five boys born to his Nigerian parents Charles and Veronica Antetokounmpo. He began playing [[youth club]] basketball with the junior teams of Filathlitikos in 2008, and then played with the senior men's team of [[Filathlitikos B.C.|Filathlitikos]] in the [[semi-professional]] [[Greek C Basket League|Greek fourth division]] (2010–11 season). ==Professional career== ===Filathlitikos (2011–2013)=== In 2011, Antetokounmpo began his [[professional sports|professional]] level career with [[Filathlitikos B.C.|Filathlitikos]], of the [[Greek B Basketball League|Greek 3rd Division]], after previously playing with the club in the Greek [[minor league]]s. During the 2012–13 [[Greek A2 Basket League|Greek 2nd Division]] season with Filathlitikos, he averaged 12.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.1 steals, and 1.0 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Thanasis_Antetokounmpo/199778?Cntry=&PlayerID=199778&stats=2013|title=THANASIS ANTETOKOUNMPO basketball profile – Season: 2012-2013 (Greece)|work=USBasket.com|access-date=March 16, 2013|language=el|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304025529/http://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Thanasis_Antetokounmpo/199778?Cntry=&PlayerID=199778&stats=2013|url-status=dead}} He was selected by the coaches to play in the 2013 [[HEBA Greek All Star Game|Greek All-Star Game]] as a special participant, even though he was not actually selected as an all-star,{{cite web|url=http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/ElladaBasket/Esake/ola-ta-asteria-sto-all-star-game.2155887.html|title=Όλα τα αστέρια στο All Star Game|date=March 16, 2013|work=Sport24.gr|access-date=March 16, 2013|language=el|archive-date=January 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127181624/http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/ElladaBasket/Esake/ola-ta-asteria-sto-all-star-game.2155887.html|url-status=live}} and competed in the slam dunk contest as players from the second division are eligible to compete in the dunk competition. After originally declaring for the [[2013 NBA draft]], he withdrew from the draft on June 17, 2013, along with 17 other players, on the day of the withdrawal deadline.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/18/2013-draft-withdrawals/|title=Regular Season Round 2: Filathlitikos – Ermis Lagkada 76-69|date=October 19, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 19, 2013|archive-date=June 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628082905/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/18/2013-draft-withdrawals/|url-status=live}} He had originally entered the draft with his younger brother [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]]. He played four games for Filathlitikos in the [[2013–14 Greek A2 Basket League|2013–14 Greek A2 League season]]. In a round 2 game against Ermis Lagkada on October 19, 2013. He recorded 15 points, 8 rebounds, 1 assist and 1 steal in his team's 76–69 win.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/18/2013-draft-withdrawals/|title=Eighteen early-entry candidates withdraw from 2013 Draft|date=June 18, 2013|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=June 18, 2013|archive-date=June 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628082905/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/18/2013-draft-withdrawals/|url-status=live}} ===Delaware 87ers (2013–2014)=== On November 1, 2013, Antetokounmpo was selected by the [[Delaware 87ers]] with the ninth overall pick in the [[2013 NBA Development League Draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2013/|title=2013 NBA Development League Draft|date=November 1, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 1, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140208013013/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2013/|archive-date=February 8, 2014}} On November 23, 2013, in his D-League debut, Antetokounmpo recorded 14 points, 2 rebounds, and 2 assists, in a 117–106 loss to the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20131123/DELCTN/gameinfo.html|title=CHARGE VICTORY SPOILS D-LEAGUE DEBUT FOR 87ERS|date=November 23, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 23, 2013|archive-date=March 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329071028/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20131123/DELCTN/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}} He also competed at the 2014 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|NBA D-League Slam Dunk Contest]]. During the [[2013–14 NBA Development League season]], he averaged 12.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.3 blocks in 50 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/antetth01.html |title=Thanasis Antetokounmpo D-League Stats |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=May 1, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150424193721/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/antetth01.html |archive-date=April 24, 2015 }} On May 1, 2014, he was named to the 2014 NBA D-League All-Defensive third team.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_development_league_all_nba_dleague_teams_2014_05_01.html|title=NBA Development League Announces 2013-14 All-NBA D-League Selections|date=May 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=May 1, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413075103/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_development_league_all_nba_dleague_teams_2014_05_01.html|archive-date=April 13, 2016}} ===Westchester Knicks (2014–2016)=== [[Image:Thanasis Antetokounmpo with Westchester.JPG|thumb|right|Antetokounmpo with the Westchester Knicks in January 2016]] On June 26, 2014, Antetokounmpo was selected with the 51st overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5848318/thanasis-antetokounmpo-new-york-knicks-nba-draft-results-2014|title=2014 NBA Draft Results: Knicks select Thanasis Antetokounmpo with 51st pick|date=June 26, 2014|work=sbnation.com|access-date=October 2, 2014|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303220042/http://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5848318/thanasis-antetokounmpo-new-york-knicks-nba-draft-results-2014|url-status=live}} He later joined the Knicks for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 3.0 points and 1.8 rebounds in five games. On November 3, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4890587|title=Westchester Knicks Finalize Inaugural Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2014|access-date=November 3, 2014|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924141746/http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4890587|url-status=live}} On April 22, 2015, he was named to the 2015 NBA D-League All-Defensive second team.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-announces-2014-15-all-league-teams/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2014-15 All-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 22, 2015|access-date=April 22, 2015|archive-date=April 26, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426012519/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-announces-2014-15-all-league-teams/|url-status=dead}} In 47 games for Westchester, he averaged 13.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.7 steals, and 1.7 blocks per game. In July 2015, Antetokounmpo re-joined the New York Knicks for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 6.4 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in five games. On August 7, 2015, he signed with the Knicks,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-thanasis-antetokunmpo|title=Knicks Sign Thanasis Antetokounmpo|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, ===Andorra (2016–2017)=== On August 8, 2016, Antetokounmpo signed with [[BC Andorra|MoraBanc Andorra]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bca.ad/antetokoumpo-energia-pura-pel-morabanc-andorra/|title=Antetokoumpo, energia pura pel Morabanc Andorra|work=BCA.ad|date=August 8, 2016|access-date=August 8, 2016|language=ca|archive-date=August 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812131937/http://www.bca.ad/antetokoumpo-energia-pura-pel-morabanc-andorra/|url-status=live}} He played an instrumental role as his team qualified for the first time in 22 years to the [[2017 ACB Playoffs|ACB playoffs]], where they were eliminated in the quarterfinals by [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. He averaged 7.3 points and 3.8 rebounds per game during regular season, before raising his contribution to 12.7 points and 4.7 rebounds in the playoffs. The Spanish basketball magazine ''Gigantes del Basket'' awarded Antetokounmpo with their 2017 "Top 5 Trophy", which goes to the [[Liga ACB]] "Most Spectacular Player of the Year".{{Cite web |url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/featured/388221/thanasis-antetokounmpo-won-spectacular-player-award-gigantes/ |title=Thanasis Antetokounmpo won the most spectacular player award of Gigantes. |date=January 23, 2017 |access-date=July 12, 2017 |archive-date=June 21, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170621093235/http://www.eurohoops.net/en/featured/388221/thanasis-antetokounmpo-won-spectacular-player-award-gigantes/ |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SgvHcEmLS6E |title=Gigante Más Espectacular: Thanasis Antetokounmpo (MoraBanc Andorra) . |website=[[YouTube]] |access-date=July 12, 2017 |language=es |archive-date=August 19, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819051508/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SgvHcEmLS6E&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live }} ===Panathinaikos (2017–2019)=== On July 11, 2017, Antetokounmpo returned to Greece and signed a two-year deal with the [[EuroLeague]] giants [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], of Greece's [[Greek basketball league system|top-tier]] level [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7xqsaspwpmsy689v|title=Panathinaikos pens Antetokounmpo on two-year deal|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 11, 2017|access-date=July 11, 2017|archive-date=October 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018230057/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7xqsaspwpmsy689v|url-status=live}} He was named [[HEBA Greek All-Star Game#All-Star Game results|the MVP]] of the 2018 [[HEBA Greek All Star Game|Greek All-Star Game]]. In June 2018, Antetokounmpo won the championship of the Greek League 2017–18 season with Panathinaikos, after beating [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]] in the league's finals, after a five-game series.{{cite web |url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-06/18/c_137261749.htm |title=Panathinaikos wins Greek Basket League Championship Final |website=Xinhuanet |date=18 June 2018 |access-date=July 14, 2022 |archive-date=August 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813022136/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-06/18/c_137261749.htm |url-status=dead }} He was named the [[Greek Basket League Most Spectacular Player|Greek League's Most Spectacular Player]], of the [[2017–18 Greek Basket League|2017–18 season]]. On February 17, 2019, he won the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]]'s [[2018–19 Greek Basketball Cup|2019 Grand Final]], after [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]] defeated [[PAOK BC|PAOK]], by a score of 79–73 in the title game, which was held in [[Heraklion Indoor Sports Arena]], on Crete.{{cite web |url=https://www.paobc.gr/en/57104_panathinaikos-bc-opap-won-2019-greek-cup/ |title=Panathinaikos BC OPAP Won the 2019 Greek Cup |publisher=Panathinaikos B.C. |date=17 February 2019 }} On June 14, 2019, Antetokounmpo was crowned the [[Greek Basket League]]'s [[2018–19 Greek Basket League|2018–19 season]] champion with Panathinaikos, for a second year in a row, after they swept [[Promitheas B.C.|Promitheas]] in the league's finals.{{Cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/heba/893363/panathinaikos-wins-38th-greek-championship-title/ |title=Panathinaikos wins 38th Greek championship title |date=June 14, 2019 |access-date=June 27, 2019 |archive-date=March 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200306130400/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/heba/893363/panathinaikos-wins-38th-greek-championship-title/ |url-status=live }}
